newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nov '96 industrial production up 11.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nov '96 industrial production up 11.8 pct.

text.p: Mexico's industrial activity in November 1996 rose 11.8 percent compared with the same month a year earlier, the 10th straight month of increases, the Finance Minstry said on Wednesday.
The result was below a forecast of 12.6 percent in a Reuters survey of 11 economists.
Industrial production in the January-November period rose 10.6 percent versus the same 11-month period in 1995, the ministry said.

In a breakdown of November 1996 versus November 1995 data, INEGI said mining activity grew 4.3 percent, including an 11 percent increase in petroleum mining and a five percent fall in non-petroleum mining. Mining increased 7.9 percent in the first 11 months of 1996, compared with the previous year.

Manufacturing activity was up 11.7 percent for November 1996, of which 18.9 percent was composed of maquiladora activity. In the January-November period the division grew 11.4 percent versus the first 11 months of 1995.

In construction, November activity registered a 17.2 percent increase over the same month in 1995 and was 10.1 percent more than the first 11 months of 1995. Most construction was in power distribution, petroleum well drilling and telephone line installation, INEGI said.
Generation of electricity, gas and water rose 6.6 percent in November compared with the same month last year and 4.5 percent in the January-November period.
